## Correction to the original framing

This issue was originally filed as *"Bound ob_raw_turns with retention,
backpressure, and saturation metrics"*, asserting that unbounded raw dialogue
is a **disk-exhaustion path** and that the #300 capacity envelope is therefore
a hard prerequisite for full-send.

**That premise was asserted, not measured, and it is wrong.**

Measured 2026-07-24 against `zz_test_raw_turns`:

| Window | Raw turns |
|---|---|
| 2 days / 6,403 turns | 8,816 kB |
| 1 month (extrapolated) | ~132 MB |
| 1 year (extrapolated) | ~1.6 GB |
| Free on volume | 1.4 TB |

At ~1.6 GB/year this is not a disk problem at any horizon that matters. And
with the retention design resolved — candidates get embeddings, raw turns get
FTS only plus a conditional ~1 week TTL (#395) — raw turns never reach a year.
Steady state is ~30 MB with no embeddings, which was the expensive part.

Blocking full-send on a capacity envelope was gating real work on a
non-problem.

## The real risk

Not disk. **Distillation falling behind ingest** — turns expiring at the TTL
before they are ever distilled, so content is lost silently.

That is a throughput alarm, not a capacity limit. The metric that matters is:

> **oldest undistilled turn age ÷ TTL**

As that ratio approaches 1, content is about to be dropped. Backlog *bytes* are
not the signal; backlog *age* is.

## Scope

- Track and expose oldest undistilled turn age per namespace.
- Alarm when the age/TTL ratio crosses a warning threshold (proposed 0.5) and
  again at critical (proposed 0.8).
- Content-free saturation metrics: ingest rate, undistilled depth, oldest
  undistilled age, distill throughput, dead-letter count.
- Backpressure on ingest **only** if the alarm proves insufficient in practice.
  No acknowledged turn is ever silently dropped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oldest undistilled age is queryable per namespace and exposed as a
      content-free metric.
- [ ] Crossing the warning and critical thresholds is observable and tested.
- [ ] Metrics expose depth/age/throughput without payloads.
- [ ] Redaction, namespace, and exact-scope controls are never bypassed under
      pressure.
- [ ] No acknowledged turn is silently dropped.

## Note

Retention/eviction itself belongs to #395 (weekly discard drain), which owns the
conditional TTL and the write into `discarded_entries`. This issue owns only the
**alarm** that distillation is losing the race.

Scope-shares with #300. Close whichever is redundant once both are specified; do
not implement the envelope twice.
